scope: Diagnostic Node fs/crypto and TypeScript module-mock instrumentation. Not a timing A/B study; do not subtract these process CPU totals or API durations to infer production speedups. CPU includes instrumentation overhead and was not resource isolated.
limitations: Node wrappers do not observe Rust native filesystem/hash work, direct system calls or internal TypeScript calls bypassing exported APIs. Node counters are not total physical disk I/O.
Read keys can include numeric file descriptors. Logical repeated bytes can be served by OS cache. Async reads do not imply CPU hashing parallelism.
createProgram API timing is not all TypeScript setup/classification/semantic time. Observed source list overlap is not proof that owning projects can share semantic environments.
No imported-memory corruption or untrusted source mutation performed by hook. Each run retains all5catalogchecks and final integrity barriers.

Published baseline and final candidate both begin with already generated valid payloads. First candidate run is retained but has a different generation starting state and is not a comparable observation.
Compiler TypeScript6.0.3 here is separate from Turbo typechecking TypeScript7 Go compiler.

records.kind: candidate first generation; not comparable initial state
